claim: Antimicrobial resistance was estimated to claim 1.27 million lives in 2019.
source: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) was estimated to claim 1.27 million lives in 2019 (Murray et al., 2022)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Murray et al., 2022

claim: Antimicrobial resistance is predicted to claim 10 million lives annually by 2050.
source: is predicted to claim 10 million lives annually by 2050 (Naghavi et al., 2024)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Naghavi et al., 2024

claim: Polymyxin-B and polymyxin-E are in clinical use.
source: Notably, polymyxin-B and -E are in clinical use, and additional AMPs are undergoing clinical trials (Rima et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Rima et al., 2021

claim: AMPs can simultaneously target different cellular subsystems including the double membrane of Gram-negative bacteria and cytoplasmic processes.
source: AMPs can simultaneously target different cellular subsystems: they target the double membrane of Gram-negative bacteria by interacting with negatively charged membrane lipids while simultaneously disrupting cytoplasmic processes such as protein synthesis, DNA replication, cell wall biosynthesis, metabolism, and cell division (Blair et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Blair et al., 2022

claim: Compared to small molecule antimicrobials, AMP resistance genes typically confer smaller increases in resistance in experimental evolution analyses, with polymyxin-B and CAP18 being notable exceptions.
source: However, compared to small molecule antimicrobials, AMP resistance genes typically confer smaller increases in resistance in experimental evolution analyses, with polymyxin-B and CAP18 being notable exceptions (Spohn et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Spohn et al., 2019

claim: Mobile resistance genes against AMPs are relatively rare and horizontal acquisition of AMP resistance is hindered by phylogenetic barriers.
source: Moreover, mobile resistance genes against AMPs are relatively rare and horizontal acquisition of AMP resistance is hindered by phylogenetic barriers owing to functional incompatibility with the new host bacteria (Kintses et al., 2019b).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kintses et al., 2019b

claim: Plasmid-transmitted polymyxin resistance constitutes a notable exception to the rarity of mobile AMP resistance genes.
source: Plasmid-transmitted polymyxin resistance constitutes a notable exception (Nang et al., 2019)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Nang et al., 2019

claim: Polymyxins are the only AMPs that have been in clinical use to date.
source: possibly because polymyxins are the only AMPs that have been in clinical use to date (Kintses et al., 2019b).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kintses et al., 2019b

claim: Phenotypic resistance to antimicrobials is known to result in negative clinical outcomes and contributes to the emergence of genetic resistance.
source: Phenotypic resistance to antimicrobials is known to result in negative clinical outcomes and contributes to the emergence of genetic resistance (Van den Bergh et al., 2017; Brandis et al., 2023; Barrett et al., 2019; Windels et al., 2019a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Van den Bergh et al., 2017; Brandis et al., 2023; Barrett et al., 2019; Windels et al., 2019a

claim: Tachyplesin is a 17 amino acid cationic β-hairpin AMP with a molecular weight of 2.27 kDa.
source: The 17 amino acid cationic β-hairpin AMP tachyplesin (2.27 kDa) (Nakamura et al., 1988)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Nakamura et al., 1988

claim: Tachyplesin displays broad-spectrum, potent antibacterial and antifungal efficacy, minimal haemolytic effect, and minimal evolution of bacterial resistance.
source: is a promising candidate AMP because it displays broad-spectrum, potent antibacterial and antifungal efficacy, minimal haemolytic effect, and minimal evolution of bacterial resistance (Spohn et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Spohn et al., 2019

claim: It has been speculated that tachyplesin simultaneously targets multiple cellular components.
source: It has been speculated that tachyplesin simultaneously targets multiple cellular components (Liu et al., 2018; Imura et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2018; Imura et al., 2007

claim: At low concentrations, AMPs induce the formation of transient pores in bacterial membranes that allow transmembrane conduction of ions but not leakage of intracellular molecules.
source: At low concentrations, AMPs induce the formation of transient pores in bacterial membranes that allow transmembrane conduction of ions but not leakage of intracellular molecules (Rima et al., 2021; Blair et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Rima et al., 2021; Blair et al., 2022

claim: Beyond a critical ratio between the AMP and membrane lipid concentrations, pores become stable, leading to leakage of cellular content, loss of transmembrane potential, and eventual cell death.
source: Beyond a critical ratio between the AMP and membrane lipid concentrations, these pores become stable, leading to leakage of cellular content, loss of transmembrane potential, and eventual cell death (Rima et al., 2021; Blair et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Rima et al., 2021; Blair et al., 2022

claim: The E. coli and Y. pestis tripartite pumps AcrAB-TolC and EmrAB-TolC confer genetic resistance against AMPs like protamine and polymyxin-B.
source: Simultaneously, tachyplesin must avoid efflux via protein pumps, such as the Escherichia coli and Yersinia pestis tripartite pumps AcrAB-TolC and EmrAB-TolC, that confer genetic resistance against AMPs like protamine and polymyxin-B (Weatherspoon-Griffin et al., 2014; Lister et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Weatherspoon-Griffin et al., 2014; Lister et al., 2012

claim: Recent discoveries have unveiled an association between reduced antimicrobial accumulation and transient phenotypic resistance to antimicrobials.
source: Crucially, recent discoveries have unveiled an association between reduced antimicrobial accumulation and transient phenotypic resistance to antimicrobials (Pu et al., 2016; Stone et al., 2020; Whittle et al., 2021; El Meouche and Dunlop, 2018; Łapińska et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Pu et al., 2016; Stone et al., 2020; Whittle et al., 2021; El Meouche and Dunlop, 2018; Łapińska et al., 2022

claim: Bacterial fluorescence due to accumulation of tachyplesin-NBD in individual stationary phase E. coli BW25113 cells increased an order of magnitude when the extracellular concentration of tachyplesin-NBD increased from 0 to 8 μg mL–1.
source: As expected, we found that bacterial fluorescence, due to accumulation of tachyplesin-NBD in individual stationary phase E. coli BW25113 cells, increased an order of magnitude when the extracellular concentration of tachyplesin-NBD increased from 0 to 8 μg mL–1 (0–3.2 μM).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript

claim: At 8 μg mL–1 tachyplesin-NBD, the single-cell fluorescence distribution displayed a median value of 2400 a.u. after 60 min treatment at 37 °C.
source: At the latter concentration, the single-cell fluorescence distribution displayed a median value of 2400 a.u. after 60 min treatment at 37 °C (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A

claim: An increase in the extracellular concentration of tachyplesin-NBD to 16 μg mL–1 revealed a noticeable bimodal distribution in single-cell fluorescence.
source: However, a further increase in the extracellular concentration of tachyplesin-NBD to 16 μg mL–1 (6.3 μM) revealed a noticeable bimodal distribution in single-cell fluorescence.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript

claim: Low accumulators have a median fluorescence of 2400 a.u. and high accumulators have a median fluorescence of 28,000 a.u. at 16 μg mL–1 tachyplesin-NBD.
source: We classified bacteria in the distribution with a median value of 2400 a.u. as low accumulators and those in the distribution with a median value of 28,000 a.u. as high accumulators (blue and red shaded areas, respectively, in Figure 1A and S1D-J).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and supplementary figures

claim: At 46 μg mL–1 tachyplesin-NBD, a bimodal distribution in single-cell fluorescence was observed with 43% of the population being low accumulators.
source: A further increase in the extracellular concentration of tachyplesin-NBD to 46 μg mL–1 (18.2 μM) still yielded a bimodal distribution in single-cell fluorescence, 43% of the population being low accumulators
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript

claim: Only 5% of the exponential phase E. coli population were low accumulators when treated with tachyplesin-NBD at 46 μg mL–1.
source: in contrast, only 5% of the population were low accumulators when tachyplesin-NBD treatment at 46 μg mL–1 (18.2 μM) was carried out against exponential phase E. coli (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of tachyplesin-NBD against exponential phase E. coli is 1 μg mL–1.
source: Notably, the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of tachyplesin-NBD against exponential phase E. coli is 1 μg mL–1 (0.4 μM) (Łapińska et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Łapińska et al., 2022

claim: The bimodal distribution of tachyplesin-NBD accumulation was present in nine E. coli clinical isolates with diverse genetic backgrounds and various AMR genes.
source: We found that the bimodal distribution in single-cell fluorescence was also present in nine E. coli clinical isolates (treated with tachyplesin-NBD at 46 μg mL–1 or 18.2 μM for 60 min) characterised by a diverse genetic background and various AMR genes, such as the polymyxin-E resistance gene mcr1 (Majewski et al., 2021 Figure 1B and C, Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C, and a citation to Majewski et al., 2021

claim: P. aeruginosa populations displayed a bimodal distribution of tachyplesin-NBD accumulation with the presence of low accumulators.
source: In P. aeruginosa populations, we observed a bimodal distribution of tachyplesin-NBD accumulation with the presence of low accumulators (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D

claim: No evidence of low tachyplesin-NBD accumulators was found in K. pneumoniae.
source: In contrast, we did not find evidence of low tachyplesin-NBD accumulators in K. pneumoniae (Figure 1E)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E

claim: Only low levels of tachyplesin-NBD accumulation were recorded in S. aureus.
source: and recorded only low levels of tachyplesin-NBD accumulation in S. aureus (Figure 1F) in accordance with previous reports (Edwards et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and a citation to Edwards et al., 2017

claim: E. coli BW25113 displayed only low accumulators of arenicin-NBD.
source: We found that E. coli BW25113 displayed only low accumulators of another β-hairpin AMP, arenicin-NBD, and only high accumulators of cyclic lipopeptide AMPs, polymyxin-B-NBD and octapeptin-NBD (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3

claim: E. coli BW25113 displayed only high accumulators of polymyxin-B-NBD and octapeptin-NBD.
source: We found that E. coli BW25113 displayed only low accumulators of another β-hairpin AMP, arenicin-NBD, and only high accumulators of cyclic lipopeptide AMPs, polymyxin-B-NBD and octapeptin-NBD (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3

claim: E. coli low accumulators treated with 46 μg mL–1 tachyplesin-NBD for 60 min at 37 °C exhibited a fluorescence distribution akin to the entire population of cells treated with 46 μg mL–1 tachyplesin-NBD at 0 °C.
source: First, we found that E. coli low accumulators treated with 46 μg mL–1 (18.2 μM) tachyplesin-NBD for 60 min at 37 °C exhibited a fluorescence distribution akin to the entire population of cells treated with 46 μg mL–1 (18.2 μM) tachyplesin-NBD at 0 °C (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4

claim: At 0 °C, antimicrobials adhere non-specifically to bacterial surfaces as the passive and active transport across bacterial membranes is significantly diminished.
source: At this low temperature, antimicrobials adhere non-specifically to bacterial surfaces as the passive and active transport across bacterial membranes is significantly diminished (Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zhou et al., 2015

claim: Post-binding peptide-lipid interactions are significantly diminished at 0 °C, but not the primary binding step.
source: Furthermore, post-binding peptide-lipid interactions are significantly diminished at 0 °C, but not the primary binding step (Eckert et al., 2006; Lehrer et al., 1985).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Eckert et al., 2006; Lehrer et al., 1985

claim: The fluorescence of high accumulators did not decrease over time when tachyplesin-NBD was removed from the extracellular environment and bacteria were treated with 20 μg mL–1 proteinase K.
source: Moreover, we found that the fluorescence of high accumulators did not decrease over time when tachyplesin-NBD was removed from the extracellular environment and bacteria were treated with 20 μg mL–1 (0.7 μM) proteinase K, a widely occurring serine protease that can cleave the peptide bonds of AMPs (Bajorath et al., 1988; Glibowicka et al., 2022; Song et al., 2021; Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4 and citations to Bajorath et al., 1988; Glibowicka et al., 2022; Song et al., 2021

claim: Tachyplesin-NBD primarily accumulates intracellularly in high accumulators.
source: These data suggest that tachyplesin-NBD primarily accumulates intracellularly in high accumulators.
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data on proteinase K treatment and temperature effects

claim: Low accumulators exhibited a significantly higher membrane-to-cell centre fluorescence ratio compared to high accumulators (p-value <0.0001).
source: Low accumulators exhibited a significantly higher membrane-to-cell centre fluorescence ratio compared to high accumulators (p-value <0.0001, Figure 1J and K)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1J and K with statistical analysis

claim: Confocal microscopy confirmed that tachyplesin-NBD is present only on the cell membranes of low accumulators and primarily intracellularly in high accumulators.
source: and confocal microscopy further confirmed that tachyplesin-NBD is present only on the cell membranes of low accumulators and primarily intracellularly in high accumulators (Figure 1—figure supplement 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6

claim: Low and high tachyplesin-NBD accumulators had similar forward and violet side scatter values.
source: We found that these two phenotypes had similar forward and violet side scatter values (Figure 1—figure supplement 7)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 7

claim: High accumulators were significantly smaller than low accumulators in the microfluidics platform (p-value <0.0001).
source: and high accumulators were significantly smaller than low accumulators in the microfluidics platform (p-value <0.0001, Figure 1—figure supplement 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 7 with statistical analysis

claim: The survival fraction of low accumulators was not significantly different from that measured for untreated cells.
source: Subsequently, we assessed the survival of each sorted sample via colony-forming unit assays and found that the survival fraction of low accumulators was not significantly different from that measured for untreated cells, whereas the survival fraction of high accumulators was significantly lower (p-value <0.0001, Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C with statistical analysis

claim: The survival fraction of high accumulators was significantly lower than untreated cells (p-value <0.0001).
source: Subsequently, we assessed the survival of each sorted sample via colony-forming unit assays and found that the survival fraction of low accumulators was not significantly different from that measured for untreated cells, whereas the survival fraction of high accumulators was significantly lower (p-value <0.0001, Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C with statistical analysis

claim: There is a strong positive semi-log correlation between tachyplesin-NBD fluorescence and PI fluorescence (r2=0.70, p-value <0.0001).
source: We found a strong positive semi-log correlation between tachyplesin-NBD fluorescence and PI fluorescence (r2=0.70, p-value <0.0001): all bacteria exhibiting PI staining had a tachyplesin-NBD fluorescence greater than 800 a.u. and were high accumulators characterised by tachyplesin-NBD localisation both on the bacterial membranes and intracellularly; by contrast, low accumulators, where tachyplesin-NBD is primarily localised on the bacterial membranes, did not stain with PI (Figure 2D–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D–G with statistical analysis

claim: All bacteria exhibiting PI staining had a tachyplesin-NBD fluorescence greater than 800 a.u. and were high accumulators.
source: all bacteria exhibiting PI staining had a tachyplesin-NBD fluorescence greater than 800 a.u. and were high accumulators characterised by tachyplesin-NBD localisation both on the bacterial membranes and intracellularly
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data on PI staining and tachyplesin-NBD fluorescence

claim: Low accumulators, where tachyplesin-NBD is primarily localised on the bacterial membranes, did not stain with PI.
source: by contrast, low accumulators, where tachyplesin-NBD is primarily localised on the bacterial membranes, did not stain with PI (Figure 2D–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D–G

claim: There is a strong positive linear correlation between the proportion of low accumulators and the population survival fraction (r2=0.98, p-value <0.0001).
source: We used the accumulation data to measure the proportion of low accumulators relative to the whole population of bacteria at increasing tachyplesin-NBD concentrations and found a strong positive linear correlation with the population survival fraction (r2=0.98, p-value <0.0001, Figure 2H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H with statistical analysis

claim: Low accumulators, which primarily retain tachyplesin-NBD on the bacterial membranes, maintain membrane integrity and strongly contribute to the survival of the bacterial population in response to tachyplesin treatment.
source: Taken together with PI staining data indicating membrane damage caused by high tachyplesin accumulation, these data demonstrate that low accumulators, which primarily retain tachyplesin-NBD on the bacterial membranes, maintain membrane integrity and strongly contribute to the survival of the bacterial population in response to tachyplesin treatment.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple experimental observations including PI staining and survival assays

claim: Principal component analysis revealed clustering of the replicate transcriptomes of low tachyplesin-NBD accumulators, the 1:1 mixture of low and high accumulators, high accumulators, and untreated control cells with a distinct separation between these groups on the PC1 plane.
source: Principal component analysis revealed clustering of the replicate transcriptomes of low tachyplesin-NBD accumulators, the 1:1 mixture of low and high accumulators, high accumulators, and untreated control cells with a distinct separation between these groups on the PC1 plane (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: The analysis revealed significant differential expression of 1,563 genes in at least one of the three groups compared to untreated cells.
source: Our analysis revealed significant differential expression of 1,563 genes in at least one of the three groups compared to untreated cells (Figure 3—source data 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from transcriptome analysis

claim: Five distinct clusters of genes were identified based on their expression profile across the three groups relative to the control population.
source: By performing cluster analysis of these genes (Glover et al., 2022; Goode et al., 2021a) (see Methods), we identified five distinct clusters of genes based on their expression profile across the three groups relative to the control population (Figure 3A, B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A, B, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2, and citations to Glover et al., 2022; Goode et al., 2021a

claim: Gene ontology enrichment revealed significant enrichment of biological processes in clusters 2, 4, and 5.
source: Gene ontology enrichment revealed significant enrichment of biological processes in clusters 2, 4, and 5 (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and D

claim: Genes in clusters 2 and 5 were downregulated to a greater extent in low accumulators.
source: Genes in clusters 2 and 5 were downregulated to a greater extent in low accumulators; genes in cluster 4 were upregulated to a greater extent in low accumulators.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from transcriptome analysis

claim: Genes in cluster 4 were upregulated to a greater extent in low accumulators.
source: Genes in clusters 2 and 5 were downregulated to a greater extent in low accumulators; genes in cluster 4 were upregulated to a greater extent in low accumulators.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from transcriptome analysis

claim: Cluster 2 included processes involved in protein synthesis, energy production, and gene expression that were downregulated to a greater extent in low accumulators than high accumulators.
source: Cluster 2 included processes involved in protein synthesis, energy production, and gene expression that were downregulated to a greater extent in low accumulators than high accumulators (see Appendix 1—table 1 and Figure 3—source data 3 for a short and complete list of genes involved in these processes, respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from transcriptome analysis

claim: Cluster 4 included processes involved in the transport of organic substances that were upregulated to a greater extent in low accumulators than high accumulators.
source: Cluster 4 included processes involved in the transport of organic substances that were upregulated to a greater extent in low accumulators than high accumulators (Figure 3B and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and D

claim: Genes encoding major facilitator superfamily (MFS) and resistance-nodulation-division (RND) efflux pump components, such as emrK, mdtM, mdtE, and mdtF, were upregulated in low accumulators.
source: Notably, genes encoding major facilitator superfamily (MFS) and resistance-nodulation-division (RND) efflux pump components, such as emrK, mdtM, mdtE, and mdtF, were upregulated in low accumulators (Appendix 1—table 1 and Figure 3—source data 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from transcriptome analysis

claim: clsB, encoding cardiolipin synthase B, was contained in cluster 2 and downregulated in low accumulators.
source: For example, clsB, encoding cardiolipin synthase B, was contained in cluster 2 and downregulated in low accumulators (Appendix 1—table 1 and Figure 3—source data 3)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from transcriptome analysis

claim: Treatment with tachyplesin-NBD caused a strong decrease in phosphatidylglycerol (PG from 37% to 3%).
source: In accordance with our transcriptomic data, we found that treatment with tachyplesin-NBD caused a strong decrease in phosphatidylglycerol (PG from 37% to 3%, i.e. the main constituent of cardiolipin), along with the emergence of lysophosphatidylethanolamines (LPE, 10%) and slight increases in PE and FA (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 3, and Appendix 1—table 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 3, and Appendix 1—table 2

claim: Treatment with tachyplesin-NBD resulted in the emergence of lysophosphatidylethanolamines (LPE, 10%) and slight increases in PE and FA.
source: In accordance with our transcriptomic data, we found that treatment with tachyplesin-NBD caused a strong decrease in phosphatidylglycerol (PG from 37% to 3%, i.e. the main constituent of cardiolipin), along with the emergence of lysophosphatidylethanolamines (LPE, 10%) and slight increases in PE and FA (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 3, and Appendix 1—table 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 3, and Appendix 1—table 2

claim: ompA, ompC, degP, mcrB, tolA, tolB, and pal were downregulated in low accumulators, and their deletion has previously been associated with increased secretion of outer membrane vesicles (OMVs).
source: ompA, ompC, degP, mcrB, tolA, tolB, and pal were downregulated in low accumulators, and their deletion has previously been associated with increased secretion of outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) that can confer resistance to AMPs and small molecule antibiotics (Murray et al., 2020; Balhuizen et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from transcriptome analysis and citations to Murray et al., 2020; Balhuizen et al., 2021

claim: nlpA, lysS, waaC, and waaF were upregulated in low accumulators, and their overexpression has been previously associated with enhanced OMV secretion.
source: Moreover, nlpA, lysS, waaC, and waaF were upregulated in low accumulators, and their overexpression has been previously associated with enhanced OMV secretion (McBroom and Kuehn, 2007; Liu et al., 2016; Appendix 1—table 1 and Figure 3—source data 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from transcriptome analysis and citations to McBroom and Kuehn, 2007; Liu et al., 2016

claim: Low accumulators displayed an upregulation of peptidases and proteases compared to high accumulators.
source: Finally, low accumulators displayed an upregulation of peptidases and proteases compared to high accumulators, suggesting a potential mechanism for degrading tachyplesin (Appendix 1—table 1 and Figure 3—source data 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from transcriptome analysis

claim: A total of 126 TFs were inferred to exhibit differential activity between low and high accumulators.
source: A total of 126 TFs were inferred to exhibit differential activity between low and high accumulators (Figure 3—source data 4 and Lee et al., 2025).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from transcription factor activity inference and a citation to Lee et al., 2025

claim: Among the top ten TFs displaying higher inferred activity in low accumulators compared to high accumulators, four regulate transport systems: Nac, EvgA, Cra, and NtrC.
source: Among the top ten TFs displaying higher inferred activity in low accumulators compared to high accumulators, four regulate transport systems, i.e., Nac, EvgA, Cra, and NtrC (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4

claim: Within just 15 min of treatment, high levels of tachyplesin-NBD accumulation were observed in all cells, placing the whole population in the high accumulator group with a median fluorescence of 15,000 a.u.
source: Strikingly, within just 15 min of treatment, we observed high levels of tachyplesin-NBD accumulation in all cells, placing the whole population in the high accumulator group with a median fluorescence of 15,000 a.u. (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A

claim: After 30 min of treatment, a subpopulation began to display lower fluorescence, and after 60 min, the low accumulator fluorescence distribution became evident with a median fluorescence of 3600 a.u.
source: However, after 30 min of treatment, a subpopulation began to display lower fluorescence, and after 60 min, the low accumulator fluorescence distribution became evident with a median fluorescence of 3600 a.u. (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A

claim: The median fluorescence of high accumulators increased from 15,000 a.u. at 15 min to 32,000 a.u. after 120 min.
source: By contrast, the median fluorescence of high accumulators increased from 15,000 a.u. at 15 min to 32,000 a.u. after 120 min (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A

claim: The entire isogenic E. coli population initially accumulates tachyplesin-NBD to high levels, but a subpopulation can reduce intracellular accumulation of the drug in response to treatment while the other subpopulation continues to accumulate the drug to higher levels.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that the entire isogenic E. coli population initially accumulates tachyplesin-NBD to high levels, but a subpopulation can reduce intracellular accumulation of the drug in response to treatment while the other subpopulation continues to accumulate the drug to higher levels.
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data on accumulation kinetics

claim: ΔqseB and ΔqseBΔqseC mutants displayed unimodal distributions of tachyplesin-NBD accumulation constituted only of high accumulators.
source: we found unimodal distributions of tachyplesin-NBD accumulation constituted only of high accumulators for both ΔqseB and ΔqseBΔqseC mutants as well as reduced numbers of low accumulators for the ΔacrAΔtolC mutant (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B

claim: The ΔacrAΔtolC mutant displayed reduced numbers of low accumulators.
source: we found unimodal distributions of tachyplesin-NBD accumulation constituted only of high accumulators for both ΔqseB and ΔqseBΔqseC mutants as well as reduced numbers of low accumulators for the ΔacrAΔtolC mutant (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B

claim: The AcrAB-TolC tripartite RND efflux system is known to confer genetic resistance against AMPs like protamine and polymyxin-B.
source: Considering that the AcrAB-TolC tripartite RND efflux system is known to confer genetic resistance against AMPs like protamine and polymyxin-B (Weatherspoon-Griffin et al., 2014; Lister et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Weatherspoon-Griffin et al., 2014; Lister et al., 2012

claim: M9 containing 30 µg mL–1 sertraline was able to prevent the emergence of low accumulators.
source: Interestingly, M9 containing 30 µg mL–1 (98 μM) sertraline (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 2), an antidepressant which inhibits efflux activity of RND pumps, potentially through direct binding to efflux pumps (Bohnert et al., 2011) and decreasing the PMF (Li et al., 2017), or 50 µg mL–1 (110 μM) verapamil (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), a calcium channel blocker that inhibits MATE transporters Radchenko et al., 2015 by a generally accepted mechanism of PMF generation interference (Rodrigues et al., 2012; Mahamoud et al., 2007), was able to prevent the emergence of low accumulators.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 2, and citations to Bohnert et al., 2011; Li et al., 2017

claim: M9 containing 50 µg mL–1 verapamil was able to prevent the emergence of low accumulators.
source: Interestingly, M9 containing 30 µg mL–1 (98 μM) sertraline (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 2), an antidepressant which inhibits efflux activity of RND pumps, potentially through direct binding to efflux pumps (Bohnert et al., 2011) and decreasing the PMF (Li et al., 2017), or 50 µg mL–1 (110 μM) verapamil (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), a calcium channel blocker that inhibits MATE transporters Radchenko et al., 2015 by a generally accepted mechanism of PMF generation interference (Rodrigues et al., 2012; Mahamoud et al., 2007), was able to prevent the emergence of low accumulators.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3 and citations to Radchenko et al., 2015; Rodrigues et al., 2012; Mahamoud et al., 2007

claim: Tachyplesin-NBD cotreatment with sertraline simultaneously increased tachyplesin-NBD accumulation levels in individual cells and the proportion of PI-stained cells.
source: Furthermore, tachyplesin-NBD cotreatment with sertraline simultaneously increased tachyplesin-NBD accumulation levels in individual cells and the proportion of PI-stained cells (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E and F

claim: The survival fraction measured after the combination treatment of tachyplesin-1 and sertraline was fivefold lower than that measured after tachyplesin-1 treatment alone.
source: The survival fraction after treatment with sertraline was comparable to that measured for untreated E. coli, whereas the survival fraction measured after the combination treatment was fivefold lower than that measured after tachyplesin-1 treatment (Figure 4G).
